title: Eli Wilner October Frame Funding Program
summary: In response to the continued demand for the program, Eli Wilner & Company funding partners have committed an additional $200,000 for the October 2026 funding cycle. These funds will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis through October 31st, 2026, or until the funds are fully committed. Eli Wilner & Company has announced that all funding allocated through its museum grant program for September 2026 has been fully committed in support of reframing and frame restoration projects at museums and cultural institutions nationwide. The grants are intended to offset a portion of the cost of qualifying frame restoration and reframing projects. title: Colby College Museum of Art announces 2026-2027 Lunder Institute Fellows
summary: Awarded to scholars, researchers and artists whose work aligns with the Lunder Institute ’s mission of expanding the boundaries of American Art, fellowships foster experimentation, research and production at all stages of practice by providing space, time and resources to incubate leading work in the field. Each fellow engages with the Colby campus community, the museum’s collection and the broader Waterville community through onsite visits with academic departments, public programs, workshops or studio visits and research using the Colby College Museum of Art’s collection. Additional information about these fellows and opportunities to engage with them on campus will be announced throughout the year. title: Festival of Arts expands Permanent Art Collection with two new acquisitions
summary: The Festival of Arts of Laguna Beach announced the acquisition of two paintings by artists who exhibited in the 2026 Fine Art Show. The newly acquired works: Moon Light by Michael Situ and Time of Reflection by Jason Li, will join the Festival’s Permanent Art Collection . Both paintings capture the beauty of Laguna Beach at distinctly different moments, from moonlight illuminating Heisler Park to the warm glow of a coastal sunset. Together, the works offer two unique interpretations of the landscape that has inspired generations of artists and helped shape Laguna Beach’s artistic identity. “These acquisitions are a wonderful reflection of the artistic excellence we see each year at the Festival of Arts,” said Christine Georgantas, Exhibits Director for the Festival of Arts. “Michael and Jason each bring their own perspective and style to the Laguna Beach landscape, and we are thrilled

title: Royal Academy of Arts announces major exhibition on the French Riviera's modern art legacy
summary: The Royal Academy of Arts presents Painting the French Riviera, a major exhibition exploring the rise and development of modern art on the Mediterranean coast of France from the 1870s to the 1960s. Bringing together over 120 paintings, sculptures and drawings, as well as film, books and travel posters, the exhibition examines how artists including Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Berthe Morisot, Henri Matisse, Pablo Picasso and Yves Klein found inexhaustible inspiration in the brilliant light, azure skies and luminous sea in the unspoilt Eden that was the South of France. Spanning nearly 90 years, the exhibition traces the transformation of the Mediterranean coast into one of the defining landscapes of modern art. More than simply a place of retreat, the Riviera came to symbolise an ideal of artistic and spiritual renewal, inspiring artists to develop

title: First major European exhibition by Salman Toor opens at the Courtauld Gallery
summary: The Courtauld presents the first solo exhibition in Europe of the artist Salman Toor, acclaimed for his arresting paintings of the contemporary experience and urban life. The exhibition brings together an outstanding selection of the artist’s most iconic, thought-provoking and at times humorous paintings, never-before-seen in Britain. Salman Toor (b.1983) was born in Lahore, Pakistan, and lives and works in New York. His paintings capture people in moments of friendship and love, as well as solitude and alienation. The exhibition at the Courtauld presents 19 paintings, all created since 2019, that focus on Toor’s exploration of human interactions and the desire and struggle to experience a sense of belonging, both culturally and emotionally. title: Major exhibition Black Bed by Katharina Grosse opens at MUNCH
summary: MUNCH is presenting a major exhibition by celebrated German artist Katharina Grosse, known for her immersive, large-scale works that transform architecture, landscapes, and interiors into vibrant fields of colour. For this exhibition Grosse created a new body of work, in dialogue with Edvard Munch and his artistic legacy. For over three decades, Katharina Grosse has challenged conventional ideas of painting. Treating the world itself as a site for painting, she applies colour directly onto buildings, objects, landscapes, and canvas, using a spray gun to extend her reach as far as her eye can see. In her work, there is no clear distinction between artwork, architecture, environment and viewer; painting can appear anywhere. At the heart of the exhibition at MUNCH is Black Bed (2026), a newly commissioned installation that revisits Grosse's seminal work Das Bett(2004). title: Dinosaurs are forever: A pictorial history of paleoart
summary: It was 1830 when an English scientist named Henry De la Beche painted the first piece of paleoart, a dazzling, deliciously macabre vision of prehistoric reptiles battling underwater. Since then, artists the world over have conjured up visions of dinosaurs, woolly mammoths, cavemen, and other creatures, shaping our understanding of the primeval past through their exhilarating images. In this book, writer Zoë Lescaze and artist Walton Ford present the astonishing history of paleoart from 1830 to 1990. These are not cave paintings produced thousands of years ago, but modern visions of prehistory: stunning paintings, prints, drawings, sculptures, mosaics, and murals that mingle scientific fact with unbridled fantasy. The collection provides an in-depth look at this neglected niche of art history and shows how the artists charged with imagining extinct creatures often projected their own aesthetic whims onto prehistory, rendering

title: British Museum presents landmark Korean art exhibition featuring Lee Kun-Hee collection
summary: A new exhibition at the British Museum explores over two millennia of Korean art and culture, offering a fresh perspective on the peninsula's rich creative history. Drawing on exceptional works from the collection of the late Samsung Chairman, Lee Kun-Hee, this is the first major exhibition on Korea's art and history at the British Museum in over 40 years. Spanning from 300 BC to the present day, Korea reveals how the country's artists and craftspeople have continually demonstrated creativity, resilience and superb technical skill, while absorbing outside influences to create a distinctive and enduring cultural identity. At a time when Korean culture has an unprecedented global presence, often described as the Korean Wave, or hallyu, this exhibition offers important context for understanding its deeper historical roots. title: Omid Delafrouz explores modern political history and territorial struggle in new Stockholm show
summary: Andréhn-Schiptjenko is presenting Omid Delafrouz's fourth solo exhibition at the gallery, Terra Nullius. The exhibition opened on Thursday 1 October. Terra Nullius means 'no man's land' in Latin. The exhibition title can be interpreted literally, but it is also a term in international law used to define the legal status of a landmass. Prior to its current judicial usage, the thought model of a 'Terra Nullius' was employed during the colonial era as a means of power to justify arbitrary occupations of already inhabited territories, where the indigenous population was often driven from their land or exterminated. title: National Museum of Natural History's Sant Director Kirk Johnson to depart for the Denver Museum of Nature and Science
summary: Kirk Johnson announced today that he will step down as the Sant Director of the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Natural History after 14 years in the role, as he prepares to join the Denver Museum of Nature and Science as its next president and CEO. An advocate for science, nature and the power of museums to influence the future, Johnson joined the National Museum of Natural History in 2012. Prior to arriving at the Smithsonian, he served as vice president and chief curator at the Denver Museum of Nature and Science. title: Berlin Municipal Galleries Art Week opens with 150 artists across the city
summary: The 2026 edition of Berlin Municipal Galleries Art Week opened today, launching ten days of exhibitions, performances, workshops and gallery tours across the German capital. Running through October 11, the event brings together 150 artists in 44 exhibitions at 36 galleries, with all exhibitions and many accompanying events offered free of charge. Organized by the network of Berlin’s municipal galleries, the program presents a broad cross-section of the city’s contemporary art scene, with exhibitions addressing memory, ecology, gender, colonial history, life after German reunification and changing ideas of beauty. Rather than following a single curatorial theme, Art Week emphasizes the range of approaches and perspectives represented across Berlin’s districts. title: Revered photographer's archive made public for the first time
summary: Experience more than 150 photographs, ephemera and working materials—all rarely or never-before exhibited—in Nancy Rexroth: Secrets of My Power, on view at the Cincinnati Art Museum from October 2, 2026, to January 3, 2027. This long overdue first retrospective marks the 50th anniversary of Rexroth’s pathbreaking work, IOWA, the influential photobook she made in the 1970s in Ohio. Nancy Rexroth (American, b. 1946) established her artistic voice in the late 1960s and 1970s, as feminism, technical experimentation, new educational opportunities and increasing interest from institutions and collectors transformed the art photography scene. While completing her MFA at Ohio University, Rexroth used a Diana camera (a low-tech device originally manufactured as a novelty) to create dream-like pictures in the small towns around Athens, Ohio. title: Slavs and Tatars curate a new exhibition on craft, labor and desire at Haus Esters
summary: The starting point for the dialogue with the internationally renowned artist collective Slavs and Tatars is the exhibition Kunst Hand Werk Brücke at Haus Lange. Having previously exhibited as artists at Haus Esters in 2019, the collective Slavs and Tatars now returns as curators with the exhibition Handdschob. In it, they explore craft as a field in which labor, sexuality, and identity intersect. Handdschob will be on view at Haus Esters from October 4, 2026, to March 7, 2027, as part of the HLHE Dialogue: Art x Crafts. Featuring nine artistic positions from seven different cultural and geographical contexts, the exhibition opens up a cross-disciplinary dialogue between historical and contemporary understandings of craft. Handdschob brings together nine contemporary artistic positions, including the curators themselves—the collective Slavs and Tatars—who are represented with their own works and have also developed the exhibition architecture. title: Rinpa painting from Edo-Period Japan is in the spotlight in exhibition at the New Orleans Museum of Art
summary: This fall, the New Orleans Museum of Art (NOMA) opens Second Nature: Japanese Rinpa Paintings from the Gitter-Yelen Collection, an immersive look at this influential tradition. One of the most distinctive schools of Japan’s Edo period (1615–1868), Rinpa artists combined specialized ink painting techniques with a shimmering, polychrome palette in compositions depicting natural scenes. Second Nature includes an extraordinary collection of nearly 60 paintings in an array of formats, including hanging scrolls, folding screens, fans, albums, and handscrolls, as well as ceramics and decorative arts, to offer new insights and perspectives into Rinpa painting and the role of artist Sakai Hōitsu in defining the style from its disparate progenitors. title: New exhibition explores Pacific Northwest forests through a century of art
summary: The Whatcom Museum announced its newest exhibition, Forested, which celebrates artists from the museum’s collection who look to the forests of the Pacific Northwest for inspiration. Of particular focus is a large selection of works by Bellingham artists Elizabeth Colborne and Helen Loggie. Orphaned as a young child, Colborne moved to Bellingham in 1890 to live with her aunt. It was the forests of Whatcom County where she developed a lifelong affection for the outdoors. For most of her adult life, she divided her time between Bellingham and New York City, where she attained a national reputation as a successful illustrator, painter, and printmaker for major publications. But it was her Pacific Northwest landscapes for which she became best known. “The Whatcom Museum is fortunate to hold the world’s largest comprehensive

title: Jenkins Johnson Gallery celebrates David C. Driskell with California survey
summary: Jenkins Johnson Gallery is presenting David C. Driskell: Wake Up Everybody, a new exhibition celebrating the creative legacy of the legendary artist, curator, art historian, and educator David C. Driskell. Featuring works created between 1960 and the early 2000s, the exhibition brings together paintings, works on paper, collage, and printmaking—including linocuts, woodcuts, and serigraphs. David C. Driskell was a lifelong artist, but he perennially prioritized the support and promotion of other artists ahead of himself. Driskell was an arts educator for nearly 40 years and a pioneering curator, but all the while he maintained a personal artistic practice which defied categorization. This exhibition samples some of his diverse areas of interest and means of expression: figuration and abstraction, Christian devotional art and traditional

title: Viktoria Binschtok explores power, surveillance and digital language in new Zwickau exhibition
summary: The Kunstverein Freunde Aktueller Kunst in Zwickau opened MEN & MEMES today, a solo exhibition by Viktoria Binschtok that looks at how images shape the way we understand power, identity and communication in contemporary life. On view through December 11, the exhibition brings together three bodies of work made between 2009 and 2026: Suspicious Minds, World of Details and Digital Semiotics. Although the series were created at different moments, they share a fascination with the visual systems that surround us—from press photography and Google Street View to emojis and memes. Binschtok’s work often begins with images that already exist. Rather than treating photography simply as a way of recording the world, she examines how pictures circulate, how they direct attention and how meaning changes when an image is removed

title: Swedenborg House opens 'Visionary Landscapes' exploring nature, mind, and memory
summary: Swedenborg House opened Visionary Landscapes, an exhibition exploring the relationship between landscape, imagination and visionary states. Curated by Museum Director Stephen McNeilly, the exhibition brings together historic works in dialogue with contemporary paintings, photography and film. Organized, in part, to showcase new acquisitions into the Swedenborg Collection, including works by William Blake, F H Evans and Francis Oliver Finch, the exhibition draws together key works from contemporary and historical artists including surrealist painter Malcolm de Chazal, occultist Austin Osman Spare, filmmaker Andrew Kötting, musician Jem Finer, photographer Jason Orton, psychogeographer Iain Sinclair, and writer Alice Albinia amongst others. title: Library of Congress celebrates 50 years of American Folklife Center with major exhibition
summary: The Library of Congress opened “Alive in Many Hands: The American Folklife Center at 50,” a new exhibition showing how living traditions carry memory, identity and community across generations. The exhibition explores traditions of music and dance, storytelling, craft, foodways, work, celebrations and everyday community life. Presented as part of a yearlong celebration of the American Folklife Center’s 50th anniversary, the exhibition brings together more than 150 objects, photographs, recordings and films to show how traditions are preserved, adapted and passed from hand to hand. Through materials spanning generations and communities, it explores how folklife connects people to one another and to the places, experiences and practices that shape them. title: From 16th-century cipher machines to bitcoin: SKD exhibition unpacks digital currency
summary: What does a 16th-century coding device have to do with bitcoin? How does the history of paper money help us understand today’s stablecoins? We come across the term “crypto” in newspaper headlines, on social media and in advertisements. But amid all the technical terms, price alerts, and dreams of fast money, it is not always clear what it is about. The exhibition “Crypto, what?” (3 October 2026 – 29 August 2027) at the Münzkabinett (Coin Cabinet) in the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden (Dresden State Art Collections, SKD) tackles an issue that is influential in our age and yet remains a mystery to many people. This is an invitation to think about digital value against a historical background of technology and money. title: TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes presents Whilst We Are Savages
summary: Whilst We Are Savages proposes a reflection on the ways in which colonial modernity constructed figures such as the savage, the barbarian, the Indigenous person and the peasant, and on the ways in which these imaginaries continue to shape how we understand territory and identity. Taking the Canary Islands as one of the earliest settings of Atlantic colonisation, the exhibition situates the archipelago within a space of dialogue between Europe, Africa and Latin America from which to address questions such as the representation of alterity, the ways in which knowledge is produced and its relationship to structures of power, extractivism, and the circulation of colonial imaginaries. title: Tchoban Foundation opens first international retrospective of anime art director Nizo Yamamoto
summary: Nizo Yamamoto – Master of Anime Scenography, at the Tchoban Foundation's Museum for Architectural Drawing, is the first exhibition anywhere outside Japan devoted to the work of the Japanese art director and artist Nizo Yamamoto (1953–2023), whose imagery ranks among the most influential in Japanese animation. Over more than four decades, Yamamoto worked with directors including Isao Takahata, Hayao Miyazaki and Mamoru Hosoda. His work on films such as Castle in the Sky, Grave of the Fireflies, Princess Mononoke and The Girl Who Leapt Through Time has made his imagery familiar to audiences the world over – though, outside Japan, his name itself has, until now, remained known only to a relatively small circle. title: Aimée Parrott explores transformation and heatwaves in 'The green fuse drives the flower'
summary: This autumn, CAMPLE LINE presents The green fuse drives the flower, an exhibition of new work by Brighton-based artist Aimée Parrott. Installed across both floors of our building, the exhibition will bring together a new body of work that offers an irresistible amalgam of painting, printmaking and textile-based techniques, through which Parrott continues to explore transitional and dual states of being and processes of transformation, transference and exchange. Monotype printing combines with dye, appliqué, staining, and stitching, producing surfaces that bear the physical imprints of time, gesture and touch. In a recent conversation with Jennifer Higgie, Parrott described her approach to making as ‘an ebb and flow, a kind of listening, paying attention. title: Kimberley Sunshine Diamond dazzles in Heritage's $7.7 million Fall Fine Jewelry Auction
summary: The Kimberley Sunshine Diamond lived up to its radiant name at Heritage Auctions' Fall Fine Jewelry Signature® Auction, where the spectacular 22.09-carat fancy yellow diamond realized $475,000 to lead a dazzling $7,707,260 event. The Sept. 28 auction drew 1,610 bidders from around the world, with spirited competition extending across white and colored diamonds, signed designer jewelry and, in one of the auction's most notable surprises, antique and period pieces. Leading them all was the Pragnell Kimberley Sunshine Diamond ring. Internally Flawless and verified as originating from South Africa's historic Kimberley Mine, the ring's showstopping center stone is secured in hand-forged 18k yellow gold talon claws, with a platinum band set with graduating rows of French- and carré-cut diamonds.
